question: Which of the following sacrificed their lives for the protection of Khejri trees?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amrita Devi Bishnoi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amrita Devi Bishnoi** was a prominent figure who sacrificed her life for the protection of **Khejri trees**. This event is popularly known as the **"Khejarli Massacre"**.
 
• The incident occurred in **1730**, when the Bishnoi community opposed the cutting of **Khejri trees** by the royal soldiers of Maharaja Abhay Singh of Jodhpur.
 
• Amrita Devi Bishnoi famously stated, "**If a tree is saved even at the cost of one's head, it's worth it**," symbolizing the Bishnoi community's commitment to environmental conservation.
 
• She, along with her three daughters and hundreds of Bishnoi people, sacrificed their lives to protect the sacred trees from being cut down. *Hence, Amrita Devi Bishnoi is the correct answer.*
 
• **Khejri trees** are considered sacred by the Bishnoi community due to their ecological importance. These trees are highly drought-resistant and contribute to the sustainability of the desert ecosystem.
 
• The sacrifice of Amrita Devi Bishnoi and the Bishnoi community is regarded as one of the earliest examples of **environmental conservation** in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Khejri Tree:**

 
 
• **Khejri** (**Prosopis cineraria**) is a drought-resistant tree native to the arid regions of India. It plays a vital role in maintaining soil fertility, providing fodder, and sustaining the desert ecosystem.
 
• It is widely revered in Rajasthan for its ecological and cultural significance. The Bishnoi community considers the tree sacred and protects it vehemently.
 
 
 
• **Bishnoi Community:**
 
 
• The **Bishnoi** community is an eco-friendly sect founded by **Guru Jambeshwar** in the late 15th century in Rajasthan.
 
• They follow 29 principles, emphasizing environmental conservation, compassion for animals, and sustainable living.
 
• **Example:** The Bishnoi community is known for protecting wildlife like blackbucks and trees like Khejri.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Conservation Legacy:**
 
 
• The sacrifice of Amrita Devi Bishnoi is commemorated as a symbol of environmental conservation and has inspired movements like the **Chipko Movement**.
 
• The Bishnoi community's efforts have contributed significantly to preserving the fragile ecosystem of the Thar Desert.
 
• The **Government of India** has recognized the Bishnoi community's efforts and commemorated their sacrifices in various ways.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legacy of Amrita Devi Bishnoi:**

 
 
• Amrita Devi Bishnoi's sacrifice is celebrated every year in Rajasthan as a mark of respect for her commitment to environmental conservation.
 
• The **Amrita Devi Bishnoi Wildlife Protection Award** was instituted by the Government of India to honor individuals or communities who contribute to wildlife and environmental conservation.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Environmental Movements:**
 
 
• Movements like the **Chipko Movement** (1970s) drew inspiration from the Bishnoi community's sacrifices.
 
• These movements emphasize the importance of **community-driven conservation efforts** to protect natural resources.
